title: Missing values in order lines
prompt: The data team's morning report says how many values are missing in each column of `order_items`. Write `solve(order_items)` so it returns one row per column with that number.
rules: One row for every column of `order_items`, even when nothing is missing in it: then `missing` is 0.
Count every row of the table, duplicates included. An empty table has 0 missing values in every column.
hints: Missing values in a column = all the rows minus the values that are there. `count()` gives the first number.
The `count` statistic of `summary` counts only the values that are there, one column at a time. It comes back as text, so turn it into a number with `int(...)`.
Loop over `order_items.columns` to build one `(name, missing)` tuple per column, then make the DataFrame with a schema string.
explanation: `order_items.count()` counts every row, while the `count` statistic of `summary` counts only the values that are there. The difference is what's missing: `filled = order_items.summary("count").first()`, then `[(c, total - int(filled[c])) for c in order_items.columns]`, built with the schema `"column_name STRING, missing BIGINT"`. Each statistic is text, so it needs `int(...)` before the subtraction. Keep columns where nothing is missing: a 0 is part of the report. Looking only at the first few rows with `head` misses gaps further down.
